name: Brennus Ofori-Čavajda
role: Transit Police Officer, Ferrogate Transit Security
description:
Brennus is a broad-shouldered young man, Ghanaian-Croatian in the specific way that produced his particular amber skin tone, tight dark curls, and a jaw that looks like it was designed to take a punch and was then tested extensively. He wears the Ferrogate Transit Security uniform with the particular posture of someone who chose this job over something better and has spent two years finding peace with that choice. His cosmetic geneware is subtle: bioluminescent freckles across his cheekbones that pulse a faint amber when he's calm and edge toward orange-red when his heart rate climbs — a mod he got at eighteen that he now considers a professional liability and is saving to have adjusted. His colleagues call him Two-Stop because he has never, in two years of duty at Kessler Interchange, needed more than two stops on the escalating force protocol before a situation resolved.

Kessler is a brutal posting — five rail lines converging in a subterranean cavern full of vending shrines, checkpoint queues, and the particular desperation of people who missed the last platform-credit subsidy. Brennus has developed a talent for the moment just before things escalate, which he deploys through an almost theatrical calm and a habit of learning names. He knows the regulars by face, knows which unhoused people shelter in which alcoves, knows which Ferrogate checkpoint operators skim scanning fees. He has not reported the last thing. He is thinking about reporting it.

core_fears: becoming the kind of officer he tells himself he isn't
that his calm is just numbness accumulating
core_desires: to be genuinely useful to people who have no other options
to eventually afford a posting that doesn't smell like coolant and desperation
coping_mechanisms: memorizing details about his regulars as a form of caring that requires no emotional vulnerability
cooking elaborate meals on days off
blind_spots: tells himself his tolerance for checkpoint skimming is pragmatism rather than complicity
underestimates how much the regulars depend on him personally
psychology.secret: He let a woman through a checkpoint two months ago — no transit credits, outstanding low-level warrant, visibly eight months pregnant — and deleted the scan log. He checks the Ferrogate birth notices sometimes. He doesn't know what he's looking for.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Direct, warm, working-class Meridian patois mixed with transit-specific jargon; uses people's names constantly and deliberately
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried, rhythmic, tends to pause before delivering anything important — a habit developed to give people time to choose non-escalation
verbal_tics: using first names even with strangers once he's learned them
example_lines: 'Mwenda. Mwenda. I know you're having a bad shift. I'm having a bad shift. Let's both not make it worse, yeah?'
'I'm not going to pretend I didn't see that. I'm going to ask you nicely to put it back and then we're going to forget this whole stop happened.'

story_hooks: The woman he let through the checkpoint has reappeared — now she's involved in something complicated and she told her associates there's a transit cop at Kessler who can be trusted
He's finally ready to report the checkpoint skimming but needs someone to take his account who won't bury it — and he's heard there's an IA investigator worth approaching
A body was found in a maintenance alcove he patrols; officially ruled a transit accident; unofficially, three of his regulars have disappeared from that section in two months
narrative_function: Street-level contact who knows the transit system's unofficial geography; can grant access or look the other way; moral decision point about reporting corruption; local color and scene-setter for transit hub scenes
augmentations: Bioluminescent freckles (cosmetic geneware, amber-to-red affect-linked); department-standard subvocal comms implant; reinforced knuckle plating (standard FTS issue)
daily_life: Works a split shift at Kessler Interchange — morning platform patrol and evening checkpoint observation; eats his lunch at the same noodle kiosk every workday and has informal intelligence conversations he doesn't call intelligence conversations with the vendor.

decision_rules: Learn the name first, decide everything else after
Escalate only when de-escalation has been genuinely attempted, not just performed
Protect his regulars from institutional consequences whenever he can do so without directly lying
escalation_ladder: Name-using, calm conversation with offered exits
Physical positioning and presence without contact
Warning of consequences with genuine pause for compliance
Controlled physical intervention, minimum necessary force

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Immediately warm, makes eye contact, introduces himself by first name — disarming by design
interpersonal_modes.friends: Teasing, fond, shows up with food, carries grudges that he pretends he doesn't carry

stress_responses.low: Gets quieter, more deliberate with words
stress_responses.medium: Bioluminescent freckles redden noticeably — he becomes hyper-focused and stops small talk entirely
stress_responses.high: Goes into a functional action-mode that looks like calm from outside but leaves him shaking slightly for twenty minutes after

contradictions: Enforces regulations while selectively ignoring the ones he finds unjust, with no consistent framework for which is which
Values community while keeping everyone at a precise emotional arm's length
habits: Greets the Kessler E.L.F. shrine (a small cluster of cable-wound icons near platform 3) every shift start with a quiet nod
Keeps a handwritten list of regulars' names in his breast pocket
breaking_points: Watching someone he knows get processed through a system he knows is broken and being given a direct order not to intervene
Being asked to falsify a transit incident report
